decisions.rationale: Exhaustive review of all 197 comparators found no feature sharing the event-driven GUI projection authority, delivery and resynchronization lifecycle, user outcome, state boundary, and failure semantics. The listed event-ordering and operational-status features are plausible projection neighbors but govern different authorities and failures.

All 197 comparators were checked; none governs the requirements-coverage dashboard's producer authority, schema identity, refresh lifecycle, truthful presentation states, and failure semantics. Dashboard grid scope and catalog authority are adjacent but separate dashboard concerns.

Review of every comparator found no strict equivalent for Planning Wizard Approve And Build project-identity derivation and CAS authority. The handoff contract is an umbrella neighbor, while the concept-thread approval status has different authority, lifecycle, and receipt failures.

All 197 comparators were considered. None matches the Planning Wizard runtime's seed, topic-operation, integration, and compare-and-swap state boundary; blocker presentation and PRD-to-Wizard handoff are related members with different outcomes and failures.

Every comparator was reviewed. Atomic GUI mutation and save-conflict races overlap one failure pattern, and context rewrite is adjacent, but none shares the preview-specific bridge allowlist, annotation authority, focus fencing, mutation lifecycle, and undo/failure boundary as a whole.

Exhaustive comparison found no strict equivalent for PreviewSession identity, transition, focus, loopback trust, restore, bridge, and CEF-bundle lifecycle. Shared-model race and multi-window lifecycle risks are plausible neighbors but have different product authority and failure boundaries.

All 197 comparators were checked. Several expose missing UI-state truth, but none owns the planning runtime UI-command companion read model with revision, asynchronous terminal state, reconnect, disabled-reason, announcement, and localization semantics.

Exhaustive review found no comparator with the same generic UICommand schema authority, enablement, stale-projection, idempotency, receipt, recovery, and cross-cutting GUI obligations. The listed concrete command and blocked-state contracts are members or consumers, not equivalents.

All 197 comparators were compared. Consumer routing, blocked-state rendering, and native renderer selection are adjacent, but none shares the unified document source authority, renderer fallback, dependency security, owner-mirror reconciliation, and Markdown/Mermaid lifecycle.

Every comparator was reviewed; none has the same runtime-artifact schema authority, consumer presentation boundary, safe-rendering lifecycle, version evolution, scale, and GUI failure semantics. Generic GUI-truth, context inspection, and receipt-backed summary concerns remain distinct consumers or neighbors.

All 197 comparators were checked. None owns local-and-remote storage-size reporting or its honesty and accessibility states; the generic graph and identity GUI-accessibility gap is related only at the cross-cutting presentation layer.

Exhaustive comparison found no match for persisted per-project panel, filter, focus, and typed deep-link context across the named surfaces. Navigation and widget-state architecture are adjacent or umbrella contracts with distinct authority, lifecycle, and failure behavior.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. Help delivery, guided-help classification, and highlighting accessibility are related, but none shares authored first-use and expert/ELI5 copy persistence with locale, fallback, precedence, versioning, and recovery authority.

Every comparator was considered. The visualizer bridge and editor-buffer recovery items are plausible members, but none combines scoped replay and shared-buffer recovery persistence with capability, sanitization, quota, integrity, conflict, and migration semantics.

All 197 comparators were checked. Dashboard grid scope, atomic/page-widget ownership, and catalog authority are adjacent, but none owns the project-scoped Usage page placement, Usage routing, ledger/chat entries, and cross-project-selector boundary.

Exhaustive review found no comparator with the Usage-widget removal, responsive, empty-state, and hover/click parity lifecycle. General adaptation, accessibility fallback, and widget manipulation are related concerns with different state boundaries and outcomes.

Every comparator was reviewed. Context inspection/rewrite and composer references share raw-content trust concerns, but neither has the Usage thread inspector's curated message projection and on-demand payload dereference authority, redaction, hostile-content, missing-ref, and access lifecycle.

Exhaustive review of all 197 comparators found no feature with the same canonical UsageRecord write path, platform window semantics, retention and rollup lifecycle, project-scope disclosure, freshness authority, and failure boundary.

All 197 comparators were considered. Default Dashboard layout and catalog/ownership rules are plausible structural neighbors, but none shares the Usage page's required widget composition, non-empty seed catalog, default layout, and analytics acceleration signal.

Every comparator was reviewed. Widget architecture and Dashboard catalog contracts are adjacent, but none combines Dashboard reuse for all Usage widgets, blocked-versus-failed recovery observability, and canonical cross-surface Ledger/Usage receipt routing.

All 197 comparators were checked. Stale browser canon retirement and provider readiness projection are related, but neither owns the UF-001 migration-only bridge plus provider missing-versus-zero, confidence, entitlement, region, overload, and capability state contract.

Exhaustive review found no comparator sharing the nine-condition UsageAnomalyGuard authority and its required decision explanation. Account-switch disclosure and blocked-family consumer semantics are presentation neighbors with different triggering state and failure outcomes.

All 197 comparators were compared. Rich-surface unavailability and blocked-subagent recovery also lack user recovery states, but neither has the exporter's degraded-status owner, propagation, diagnostics, alerting, GUI truth, and localization lifecycle.

Every comparator was reviewed. The listed items likewise reject visual or fixture claims as production truth, but they govern metadata, thread status, success receipts, or promotion evidence rather than the web-card content, lifecycle, accessibility, localization, and recovery boundary.

All 197 comparators were checked. The YOLO authority toggle and mode/model selector contract are plausible neighbors, but neither resolves web-card injection behavior for the regular and yolo runtime modes or its omission semantics.
Exhaustive review of all 197 comparators found no feature with the same source-packet receipt schema authority, packet identity, and minimum-four-file manifest cardinality contract.

All 197 comparators were considered. The other machine-readable receipt also correctly excludes GUI concerns, but it is a different certification authority and receipt lifecycle; shared non-applicability does not satisfy product-authority equivalence.

Every comparator was reviewed. Fixture non-evidence and promotion gating are governance neighbors, but neither owns the versioned web-operation fixture corpus or its delegated WebOperationCard schema validity lifecycle.

All 197 comparators were checked. CTA cards have a separate shared-field contract, but no comparator shares the ten-scenario positive web-operation fixture catalog, its owner authority, scenario outcomes, and validation boundary.

Exhaustive review found no equivalent for the running research card's phase, counters, elapsed/remaining time, cancellation, partial-result, and invariant boundary. Operational thread status is a different projection authority and lifecycle.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. File-operation and message interruption cancellation are related lifecycle patterns, but neither represents a cancelled crawl retaining page counts, elapsed time, and partial-output lineage.

Every comparator was checked. Requested-versus-effective runtime disclosure and provider readiness are adjacent, but neither has the web-operation adapter fallback authority, structured summary, and visible collapsed-label outcome.

All 197 comparators were compared. Build-approval thread status is a plausible approval neighbor, but it differs from a pending Planning Wizard fetch gated by one-time host-scoped approval, including command state and failure semantics.

Exhaustive review found no comparator with the denied web-operation card's denial reason, authority source, and allowed recovery-action metadata. Block-family and disabled-control recovery contracts are related but govern different state boundaries.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. Routed-owner, fallback, and release-oracle accessibility gaps are related cross-cutting concerns, but none shares the web-operation fixture coverage boundary for localization keys, long/RTL text, accessible naming, and label-data disagreement.

Every comparator was considered. GUI consumer drift, cross-document UI handoff, and production-promotion evidence are related governance seams, but none identifies the missing runner and downstream consumer binding for this web-card fixture corpus.

All 197 comparators were checked. Graph, shell, and fan-out limits are scale neighbors, but none governs zero, maximum, overflow, and very-large cardinality fixture coverage for web-operation batches and crawls.
Exhaustive review of all 197 comparators found no feature with the same invalid web-card fixture authority and expected error-code, schema-path, failing-invariant, and diagnostic-outcome contract.

All comparators were reviewed. Attempt-counter exclusivity and fan-out count consistency are plausible arithmetic/concurrency neighbors, but neither has the web batch card's per-item reconciliation, lifecycle, and aggregate counter state boundary.

Every comparator was considered. Transition matrices, overlay combinations, and panel-state modeling are related consistency problems, but none binds WebOperationCard kind to card state, terminal outputs, and errors under the same authority and lifecycle.

All 197 comparators were checked. Remediation ancestry and file-operation cancellation concern retained outcomes, but neither defines a PM-composed crawl timeout distinguished from cancellation while preserving a partial-result reference.

Exhaustive review found no strict equivalent for the fixture file's missing executable callers, downstream consumers, scale envelope, and GUI presentation oracle. Consumer-drift and promotion gates are adjacent governance concerns, not the same fixture boundary.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. Policy remap/fallback and browser network-loss contracts are related, but neither owns plan/deep-plan web-card visibility, ask/deny decisions, network_blocked_by_policy, and deep_plan-to-plan normalization.

Every comparator was checked. Rich-surface unavailability and browser/network-loss work are adjacent, but neither shares browser-unavailable remediation identifiers, visible-card recovery transitions, fallback authority, retained state, accessibility, and terminal-failure semantics.

All 197 comparators were considered. Evidence revocation and receipt-backed success summaries are provenance neighbors, but neither governs planning-research claim-to-source binding, stable identity, excerpt verification, freshness, and citation-failure presentation.

Exhaustive review found no equivalent for RunModeAssertion normalization, overlay precedence, network-policy-to-decision, and decision-to-card coupling. Policy fallback and selector compatibility are adjacent inputs with different authority and outcomes.

All comparators were reviewed. Graph and fan-out scale limits are related capacity concerns, but none owns inconsistent CrawlPolicyAssertion versus NegativeCase depth/page bounds and uncapped crawl resource semantics.

Every comparator was checked. Generic GUI truth, thread status, LSP readiness, and remote freshness are close presentation analogues, but none owns web-provider registry row state-to-GUI mapping, stale-health warnings, localized labels, and accessible status reasons.

All 197 comparators were reviewed. Firecrawl UI handoff conformance is a provider-integration neighbor, but no comparator shares the Jina row's singular MCP reference versus multiple Claude/Cursor example projections and cardinality failure.

Exhaustive comparison found no strict equivalent for the provider-projection artifact's missing generator, installer, reconciler, UI, support, telemetry consumers, and accessible localized GUI truth. The listed ownership, drift, freshness, and promotion gaps are distinct seams.

All 197 comparators were checked. Event ordering and fan-out scale are related collection concerns, but neither owns provider projection uniqueness, deterministic ordering, cardinality, timeout/resource ceilings, completeness, and duplicate-tuple behavior.
